newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude dips in thin volumes.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude dips in thin volumes.

text.p: IPE July Brent ticked into negative territory on very thin volumes on Wedensday. But brokers said the market was supported around current levels following the release of weekly U.S. stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute and EIA
"The problem is a lack of liquidity. The volumes are dreadful. Some locals and small brokers have sold it down on a few lots," one broker said.
July Brent traded down one cent at $19.99 a barrel, off the intraday low of $19.95. Just over 3,600 lots had traded on the contract by 1340 GMT.
Brokers added that the market could go either way once the NYMEX opens.
"This is not a true crude futures market. We know the funds are heavily involved so it could go either way. But Brent (crude) does look somewhat supported after the API's," he added.
The API's showed a crude draw in U.S. stocks of almost six million barrels for the week ending May 16 while EIA saw a draw of 5.4 million barrels in the same period.
The crude draw in the API's represents a rise in U.S. crude stocks of 600,000 barrels since the beginning of May.
U.S. based analysts said the main focus was on the fact that stocks were some 20 million barrels higher than the same time last year.
June gas oil on the IPE was last done down 25 cents at $177.50 a tonne, again in unexciting volume trade.
"The market is just about dead," another broker said.
